workstream: U20 -- first nominal-locomotion training experiment (ARS baseline)
algorithm: Augmented Random Search (ARS-V2, Mania et al. 2018), numpy-only linear policy
note: Both runs used seed=0 (train_ars.py's default; not overridden) -- single-seed only. Multi-seed comparison is planned for the PPO baseline (U21), not repeated here retroactively.

run1.description: First full-scale run, reward v2 (alive bonus added, w_vel still 1.0 from the original design). Converged to a safe 'never move' local optimum -- see docs/rl_environment_notes.md U20 run log.
run1.reward_version: v2_alive+vel1 (pre-dates the reward_version field added later in cara_env.py; w_alive=1.0, w_vel=1.0)
run1.reward_audit_verdict: FAIL (10.0% margin of intended behavior over standing -- see reward_audit.py --w-vel 1.0)
run1.eval_summary: standing (vx=0): FELL at 0.54s. forward-walk (vx=0.10, its own trained target): survived full 4s, verdict NOT WALKING (zero forward progress) -- fall rate 1/2.

run2.description: Same hyperparameters as run1, reward v3 (w_vel raised 1.0->10.0 after run1's collapse-to-standing was diagnosed). Does not collapse to standing, but does not find a stable gait either -- falls consistently around step 20-30 of a 200-step episode.
run2.reward_audit_verdict: PASS (100.8% margin of intended behavior over standing -- see reward_audit.py, default weights)
run2.eval_summary: standing (vx=0): FELL at 0.46s. forward-walk (vx=0.10): FELL at 0.44s. fall rate 2/2. forward_walk_fall.gif shows the actual topple (verified frame-by-frame after two encoder bugs were fixed in gif_writer.py).

net_assessment: See docs/rl_environment_notes.md U20 section for the full writeup. Neither run meets the 'repeatable forward stepping' milestone. The reward-incentive bugs found along the way (missing alive bonus; vel/alive imbalance) are fixed and audited (reward_audit.py); nothing points at morphology or actuator tracking as the blocker. Preserved here as the ARS baseline before adding a nonlinear PPO baseline (U21) per explicit instruction to keep ARS as the first benchmark rather than spending substantially more compute on it.
